title: Place value & regrouping
blurb: Where a digit sits, and how tens trade with ones.

place.name: Place value
steps: Hundreds sit one more seat to the left.
place.exception: The digit alone is not the value. The 4 in 340 means 4 tens, which is 40.

carry.name: Adding with regrouping
carry.phrase: Ten ones make a ten. Carry the one next door.
steps: If you get 10 or more, keep the ones digit and carry 1 ten.
Add the tens, plus the carried ten.
carry.exception: Only carry when the ones make 10 or more. 23 + 14 has nothing to carry.

borrow.name: Subtracting with regrouping
borrow.phrase: More on top? No need to stop. More on the floor? Go next door and get ten more.
borrow.also: Numbers the same? Zero’s the game.
steps: If the bottom digit is bigger, borrow a ten from next door.
The top ones digit gets 10 more. The tens digit goes down by 1.
borrow.exception: Never flip the ones to subtract the small digit from the big one. 52 − 27 is 25, not 35.

evenodd.name: Even and odd
evenodd.phrase: Even numbers share fair: everyone gets a buddy. Odd numbers leave one out.
evenodd.also: Only the last digit decides: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 are even. 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 are odd.
steps: Look at the last digit only.
evenodd.exception: Ignore the other digits: 58 is even, even though 5 is odd. And 0 is even, because zero splits into two equal teams of nothing.

round.name: Rounding to 10 and 100
round.phrase: Five or more, raise the score. Four or less, let it rest.
steps: Find the digit you are rounding to.
Look at the digit just to its right.
5 or more: your digit goes up 1. 4 or less: it stays.
round.exception: Look only at the very next digit. 349 to the nearest hundred is 300, because the tens digit is 4. Don’t round twice (349 → 350 → 400). A 9 that goes up rolls over: 97 rounds to 100.

clock.name: Telling time
clock.phrase: Hour is a short word: short hand. Minute is a long word: long hand.
clock.also: The long hand counts by 5s: the number it points to × 5 is the minutes.
steps: Short hand: the last number it has passed is the hour.
Long hand: the number it points to × 5 is the minutes.
Say the hour, then the minutes: 3:25.
clock.exception: After half past, the short hand is close to the next number, but the hour hasn’t changed yet: at 2:50 it is almost at 3, and it is still 2. The long hand on 12 means 0 minutes, o’clock.

add3.name: Adding three numbers
add3.phrase: Hunt for a ten first, then add the last one.
steps: Look for two numbers that make 10.
add3.exception: You can add in any order, but use all three numbers. If no pair makes 10, look for a double, or just add from left to right.

month-knuckles.name: Knuckle months
month-knuckles.phrase: Knuckles are 31-day months; valleys between are shorter.
steps: Make two fists side by side.
Knuckle months have 31 days; valleys between are shorter.
After July, continue on the other fist starting at August.
February is the special short month.
month-knuckles.exception: February is 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. After July continue onto the other fist at August.

thirty-days-hath.name: Thirty days hath…
thirty-days-hath.phrase: Thirty days hath September, April, June, and November.
steps: Remember the four 30-day months: September, April, June, November.
Except February: 28, or 29 in a leap year.
thirty-days-hath.exception: All the rest have 31, except February (28, or 29 in a leap year).

commute2.name: Commutative property
commute2.phrase: Commuting either way: a + b = b + a, and a × b = b × a.
steps: For + or × the answer stays the same.
Use the swap to start with a friendlier number.
commute2.exception: Subtraction and division do not commute.

assoc2.name: Associative property
assoc2.phrase: Associate means regroup: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).
assoc2.also: Same idea for multiply: group friendly factors first.
steps: Look for a pair that makes 10 or a known fact.
Then finish the sum or product.
assoc2.exception: You may regroup, but don’t change the numbers. And − / ÷ are not associative.

wordadd2.name: Story problems: add
wordadd2.phrase: Altogether, in all, combined, sum — add the parts.
wordadd2.exception: “Sum” is addition. “Difference” is subtraction — don’t mix the words.

wordsub2.name: Story problems: subtract
wordsub2.phrase: Left, remain, fewer, take away, difference — subtract.
wordsub2.exception: “Fewer than” compares. “Left” takes away from a whole. Line up ones under ones.

wordmul2.name: Story problems: multiply
wordmul2.phrase: Each, groups of, rows of, times — multiply equal groups.
steps: Count groups × size of a group.
wordmul2.exception: Unequal groups are addition, not a single multiply.

worddiv2.name: Story problems: divide
worddiv2.phrase: Share, split equally, how many in each, how many groups — divide.
steps: Find how many groups or how many per group.
worddiv2.exception: Ask which question: size of each share, or number of shares?

estimate2.name: Estimate sums
estimate2.phrase: Round both, then add — a friendly estimate.
steps: Round each number to the nearest ten.
estimate2.exception: Both rounding up can overshoot. Use estimate to check exact work, not replace it when you need exact.

mental10.name: Mental math with tens
mental10.phrase: Add tens to tens, ones to ones — then combine.
steps: Split each number into tens and ones.
mental10.exception: If ones make 10 or more, regroup into an extra ten.

expanded.name: Expanded form
expanded.phrase: Expanded form shows what each seat is worth.
steps: Add the values with plus signs.

factfam.name: Fact families
factfam.phrase: A fact family: two adds and two subtracts from the same three numbers.
steps: List the three numbers (two parts and a whole).
factfam.exception: If two numbers match (doubles), the family is smaller — fewer unique sentences.

half2.name: Halves
half2.phrase: Half means split into two equal shares.
steps: Half of an even number is a whole number.
half2.exception: Half of an odd count leaves a remainder — you can’t split 7 apples into two equal whole apples without cutting.

compare3.name: Comparing three-digit numbers
compare3.phrase: Compare from the left: hundreds first, then tens, then ones.
steps: If still tied, look at ones.
compare3.exception: A bigger digit on the right doesn’t win if a left seat already decided it: 199 < 201.

moneycent.name: Coins to a dollar
moneycent.phrase: 100 cents make a dollar. Count coin jumps.
steps: Know values: quarter 25, dime 10, nickel 5, penny 1.
moneycent.exception: Four quarters make a dollar — not four dimes.

skip2.name: Skip-count to multiply
steps: The landing number is the product.
skip2.exception: Keep every hop the same size. Uneven hops break the multiply story.

identity2.name: Identity properties
identity2.phrase: Add 0, stay you. Multiply by 1, stay you.
identity2.exception: × 0 is not identity — it wipes the number to 0.

distrib2.name: Distributive sneak peek
distrib2.phrase: Distribute means give to everyone inside the brackets.
distrib2.also: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c.
steps: See a number outside brackets with a sum inside.
Multiply the outside by each inside part.
distrib2.exception: Distribute over + or − inside. Don’t distribute a sum outside like (a + b) × c by adding first wrongly into multiply — actually (a+b)×c is fine either way, but a+(b×c) is not a(b+c).
